items.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020
items.q: So you can hear Dexter Gordon, a single note and you know that it’s Dexter Gordon

ctx.x: Well I had a thought, speaking of the fellows over my shoulder, that era of musician placed a huge amount of importance on being able to recognize people by their personal sound. So I have an opinion, and I’ll be happy for you to tell me I’m wrong. And that is, I would — it seems to me that recognizing wind instruments, because of all the things that go into the sound — the reed, the breath, the diaphragm, the mouthpiece — would be somewhat easier than to identify vibes players because you have metal and a…

Well obviously there’s a reason why there’s not a really long lineage of great vibe players. It’s a tough instrument. It’s one of the easiest instruments to start with. I mean you basically walk up to the thing and you hit is and you get a note that’s in tune. It’s a little more complicated than that of course, but I think initially it’s one of the easier instruments to start with, compared to a trumpet for example. But then the challenge is, because you don’t have all these interesting levels of expression from…

itself, you actually have to push more of your personal expression through the instrument to make your own voice. So you can hear Dexter Gordon, a single note and you know that it’s Dexter Gordon or Lester Young. Whereas the vibraphone it’s a little harder to tell from a single note, although touch has a lot to do with it. Some people, I play with a little bit — well I play with a wide range of touch but in general I have a little bit heavier touch than let’s say Bobby Hutcherson who does a really light, sort of…
